items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 15 at 3:09PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
An east-moving wave will bring with it low temperatures reaching
into the lower 30s, and chances of light freezing rain or drizzle
for the NE Arctic Coast, including locations like Kaktovik and
Point Thomson. Any accumulations are expected to remain minimal,
with conditions improving through the daytime hours on Thursday.
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 15 at 1:28PM AKDT until July 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 40 mph
expected.

* WHERE...White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River,
including the Steese Highway summits.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 1 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down.
items.areas: White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 15 at 1:27PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
A glacier dammed lake outburst from Summit Lake continues on the
Salmon River near Hyder. Water levels on the Salmon River are
expected to continue to rise over the next day or two with an
expected crest sometime later today or Thursday. It is unknown how
much water will be released from Summit Lake which results in large
uncertainty on crest height and timing.

Potential impact area for this event is the road from Hyder to
Premier, Canada at around mile point 9 along the Salmon River.

Be aware

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 14 at 2:49PM AKDT until July 16 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water could enter several cabins along the Yentna River near Lake
Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 237 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding is expected to begin shortly, especially along the
Yentna River near Lake Creek. Addition
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
